issues.title: runtime: native code cannot read record field annotations of a resource parameter's declared type
issues.output:
corpus/extern harness (go test ./corpus/extern -run TestReproParamFieldAnnotations -update):
[id@meta]
h []
issues.reasoning: Reproduced with the issue's corpus/extern harness test on main: the typedesc path prints [id@meta] but the resource-parameter path prints 'h []'. extern.Parameter (runtime/extern/handle.go) carries only a semtypes.SemType, so natives can't reach a parameter's declared record field annotations. This is a runtime/extern API gap, not a spec question. The standalone .bal fails with 'function not found: describe' only because the externs need the Go harness.

issues.title: runtime: types lose their declared names (conversion errors, typedesc printing, native access)
issues.output:
'{| json... |}' value cannot be converted to '{| age: int, name: string, never... |}': field 'age' not present in value
'"BLUE"' value cannot be converted to '"GREEN"|"RED"'
typedesc
issues.reasoning: Reproduces exactly as described. The spec leaves conversion-error text and a typedesc's string form implementation-defined (clean-context check). Still, runtime TypeDesc values keep no declared type name: errors print types structurally, a typedesc prints as bare 'typedesc', and natives have no Type.getName() equivalent. That is a real runtime gap blocking the http port. Possibly related to #1350 (error type name printing).

issues.title: interpreter: method annotations never reach BIR and cannot be read from native code
issues.output: help
issues.reasoning: The program runs ('help'), but bir.BIRFunction has no annotations field (bir/model.go: only parameters and class defs carry Annotations), and extern.FunctionMetadata exposes parameter annotations only. Method annotations are therefore dropped before BIR and can't be read by natives. This is a runtime/extern API gap; birgen must carry the values too. Related to #1355 and #1360.

issues.title: [Bug]: query `limit` clause keeps pulling frames through `where` after the limit is reached
issues.output:
w1
s1
w2
w3
[1]
error: divide by zero
        at main(1392_0.bal:28)
issues.reasoning: Reproduced: w2 and w3 are printed after the limit is reached, and the second query panics with divide by zero. The clean-context check (§6.35 lazy pull, §6.35.6 limit) expects w1, s1, [1], [1]. It noted a minor wording ambiguity but concluded that the lazy-pull model rules out pulling more frames. The limit is desugared into a counter over the materialised rows (desugar/query_expression.go applyQueryLimitClauseToRows), so the generated code is wrong, which makes this a front-end (desugar) issue. Related to #1129.

issues.title: [Bug]: list const-pattern in `match` narrows a mutable target to the constant's type (unsound)
issues.reasoning: Reproduced: the program compiles and prints [1,2]. The clean-context check says line 10 must be a compile error: by §7.21.2, the target narrows to T &ro L, which keeps the whole mutable int[] part, and int[] is not a subtype of [1, 2]. This is unsound narrowing in the type checker.

issues.title: frontend: wildcard clause after an exhaustive enum match is rejected
issues.reasoning: Not a bug. The clean-context spec check (§7.21.2 match clause reachability plus §7.4.3: a statement other than panic that is not reachable is a compile error) found that the `_` clause after START/END covers no remaining part of the target type Context, so its `return "invalid";` is unreachable and the program must be rejected. Nutcracker's current rejection matches the spec; jBallerina accepting it is not authoritative. The ballerina/yaml port should drop the wildcard arm, or use a panic statement, which is allowed to be unreachable.
issues.close_reason: Works as specified: by spec §7.21.2/§7.4.3 the wildcard clause after an exhaustive enum match is unreachable, so it's a compile error. Drop the arm or make it a `panic`.

issues.title: frontend: distinct over a union of error types is rejected
issues.output:
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: only object and error types can be distinct
 --> 1375_0.bal:7:17
  |
7 | type InputError distinct (ParseError|FormatError);
  |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Not a bug in the rejection itself. The clean-context check found that `distinct T` requires T to be definite. ParseError|FormatError induces different type-id sets, so it is not definite and line 7 is a compile error. Line 10 is also invalid: a ParseError value lacks InputError's fresh type-id, so it isn't a subtype of InputError, and the issue's expected output is wrong. Nutcracker rejects the program correctly. Its wording ('only object and error types can be distinct', reported as SYNTAX_ERROR) is misleading but not wrong in outcome; consider a follow-up on the message. Note that the ported public type `distinct (io:Error|file:Error)` is invalid under the spec.
issues.close_reason: Works as specified: distinct requires a definite type, and a union of distinct error types is not definite (spec distinct-type-descriptor), so rejecting it is correct. The diagnostic wording could be improved separately.

undetermined.reasoning: Reproduced: 'unused variable i' for a foreach loop variable that is never read (`foreach int i in 1 ... 2`). The spec mandates no unused-variable diagnostics; nutcracker reports unused locals as errors by design (#1155). Whether a foreach binding counts is a project policy decision, not a spec question. The binding really is unused, and `foreach int _ in ...` is an available workaround. If the policy exempts loop variables (as jBallerina does), it's a frontend fix; otherwise close. Best tracked under #1155.
